method: Independent atomscan and cleave facts on each original path, decoded-string inspection, PE carving with pefile, Rizin control-flow review, Capstone decoding to bypass string annotations, and ILSpy decompilation. No specimen code was executed. ML scores, collector filenames and AV labels did not determine the verdict.

stormattack_evidence: The two originals have byte-identical .text, SHA256 98f975dd8b8d9f2e6da736754ef8f87a112e7f7e5f4d104b3f5e385e525c70c4, and the same embedded DLL at file 0x5060, length 0x9c00, SHA256 e58dd623e688da935eb785985f0c55ed8df09bd57567d8a2f6fdc10bf41511e1. Each original was scanned and hashed independently.

Outer CRT entry 0x402674 calls dispatch 0x401cb0. Configuration DWORD at file 0x4120 is 3 in both, selecting Active Setup self-copy at 0x401900, then self-delete 0x401390. Other dispatch branches implement service installation and resource-DLL injection; these are capabilities, not proof they ran in mode 3.

0x401900 creates an HKLM Active Setup Installed Components key and supplies the StubPath value-name pointer and REG_EXPAND_SZ type to RegSetValueExA at 0x401a4b. It reads its image, patches mode/path configuration, writes a copy via CRT I/O, and starts that copy. 0x401390 builds COMSPEC /c del against its own short path and starts a shell.

0x401150 launches an IE/notepad/calc target and calls VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory and CreateRemoteThread using resolved Kernel32!LoadLibraryA and a remote DLL-path buffer. 0x401260 replaces the LanmanServer ServiceDLL registry value. Resource extraction 0x402460 passes bytes to file writer 0x4023c0.
Embedded DllMain path 0x10007176 starts a worker at 0x10006922. The worker repeatedly calls connector 0x10006974, sends a STORM-formatted host report and invokes receiver 0x10006ac9.

At 0x10006b45 recv reads up to 0x528 bytes, positive length gates copying the record, and its leading DWORD selects tasks. Task 5 directly calls 0x100067c2 with a field of the received record. That helper resolves URLDownloadToFileA at 0x100068d9, downloads at 0x100068ed and launches the same local path through CreateProcessA at 0x10006917.

Raw flood routine 0x1000228e calls WSASocketA(AF_INET=2, SOCK_RAW=3, IPPROTO_UDP=17), constructs a target sockaddr and sends twelve datagrams per burst at 0x10002356..0x10002372, sleeps, then checks the stop flag and repeats. This is direct raw-UDP flooding; a DNS-labelled banner alone does not establish DNS reflection.

Embedded cleanup 0x10006665 reads StubPath, deletes the installed file and Active Setup key, and in its alternate branch restores ServiceDLL before removing a service. The only RegSetValueExA call there, 0x10006763, targets ServiceDLL. Active Setup names plus an unrelated registry writer falsely suggested persistence in this DLL.
go_and_gravityrat_evidence: The outer x64 Go binary contains Base64 and repeated raw managed payloads. Base64 begins at original file 0x2ca8cf, explaining a decoded PE reported at that offset despite no literal MZ there. A raw LSASS executable begins at 0x599e08, length 0xa1400, SHA256 1c0ea462f0bbd7acfdf4c6daf3cb8ce09e1375b766fbd3ff89f40c0aa3f4fc96.

Go main 0x62d190 obtains its module path and self bytes. visit at 0x62c450 handles walked files, reads the selected path, calls get_self_mutated_bytes at 0x62c626, and overwrites the original path with ioutil.WriteFile at 0x62c679. It appends random padding/generation marks and also writes a .exe companion at 0x62c7aa.

get_self_mutated_bytes at 0x62cf80 Base64-decodes the embedded managed executable at 0x62cfc8 and appends it plus random padding to a self-derived byte slice. plant_start_up at 0x62cba0 builds random System32 .exe names, writes generated copies, and calls add_startup. add_startup at 0x62cae0 opens HKLM Software/Microsoft/Windows/CurrentVersion/Run and calls registry.Key.setStringValue at 0x62cb72.

Go main also sends generation/hash/seed/path metadata in an HTTP GET to a Pipedream endpoint and uses randomized RequestBin subdomains. This corroborates the propagation bookkeeping but is not, alone, the reason for conviction.

ILSpy identifies the managed payload as assembly LSASS 1.9.1201.10. Program.Main initializes storage, registers an AssemblyResolve handler and enters Services.Start. The resolver reads a resource named after a requested assembly and returns Assembly.Load(bytes); its embedded Mono.Cecil dependency is ordinary library bundling, not evidence of a hostile reflective payload chain.

Services.Start selects a server from configured msoftupdates.com/.eu hosts and starts jobs and a five-minute task timer. Manager.UpdateServer parses remotely supplied tasks. RunCmd passes task.Args to CmdManager.Start, which calls hidden cmd.exe /c, saves output and invokes UploadManager. Agent.UploadFileTaskAsync sends files to /GX/GX-Server.php with the victim signature.

StartU starts a Win32_LogicalDisk creation watcher. Its handler enumerates selected files on the new volume and copies them to a local U storage directory. A ten-minute timer uploads that staging directory and deletes staged copies on successful transfer. DriveScan and DriveUpload separately enumerate and upload host files. This establishes remote command execution and unauthorized collection/export, rather than a legitimate dependency tool.

No keyboard recorder appears in the decompiled LSASS payload. The native writeKeyLog token is Go TLS key-log support, combined by the old rule with unrelated managed DoViaCmd and UploadFileTaskAsync tokens. It does not establish keyboard capture.

Unmodified Mono.Cecil at 0x5f5440, length 0x44800, SHA256 46c2fab4dc6673447d5651ecfaeb793b49a908344f193b54f63ce531fc2c16f5, decompiles as Mono.Cecil 0.9.6.0. The damaged image at 0x83b127 has a Cecil header but its CLR metadata root is overwritten with copied RAT bytes. ILSpy rejects it. A .text-only family signature still falsely matched those copied bytes; binding to parsed #Strings and #US heaps fixes that.

The scanner label Mono.Cecil.dll on the LSASS payload is a container-identification limitation: the executable embeds that library and the recovered assembly/version metadata identify the executable as LSASS. YAML traits now distinguish the actual payload from the library and damaged carrier.
judgment_context: All three are MALICIOUS on code evidence: the small files implement covert persistence/injection and operator-controlled DDoS/download execution; the large file overwrites other files, plants randomized logon copies and carries a file-exfiltrating RAT. Original distribution, user authorization and deployment histories are unavailable. Malformed/dumped or generation-mutated bytes can impair execution; no successful infection, live C2 or current server ownership is claimed.
changes: Removed hostile resource/AppDomain/reflection co-occurrence: a benign compiled dependency resolver meets its conditions. Existing neutral resource, CLR, reflection and module-load observations remain.

Replaced the redundant Active Setup/StubPath/write-API co-occurrence aggregate with a notable, section-scoped x86 instruction matcher that binds the pushed StubPath pointer and the RegSetValueExA IAT slot. Both persistence consumers require the actual write plus Active Setup context.

Removed the cross-component keylogging family rule and generic UploadFile/DoViaCmd identity pair. Retained GravityRAT GX identity is bound to the current image parsed CLR #Strings/#US heaps; incidental resource, overlay and damaged-Cecil strings do not satisfy it.

external_corroboration.use: Talos describes GX remote-command/file-exfiltration capabilities and msoftupdates infrastructure. Family corroboration only; all local effects above were traced independently.

resource_loader_control: An unsigned net8 library compiled from DependencyResolver.cs with deterministic random.Random(581) 128 KiB resource data has every old all-leg. GetMethods matches its old any-leg via test-rules; it is stripped from ordinary output as an unreferenced component after removal of the hostile consumer. The control has no suspicious or hostile finding.
validation: make validate must be the final operation; regenerate staged YARA only if it reports a stale precompile fingerprint.
